docs.title: ArqonPilot
docs.text:
ArqonPilot is a production CLI for single-repo and cross-repo engineering operations: Oracle indexing/query, healing, branch orchestration, release navigation, security workflows, planning, scaffolding, and knowledge capture.

ArqonPilot is designed for high-control operation: - dry-run first for mutating commands - explicit repo targeting (group/tag filters) - auditable output for cross-repo actions

docs.title: 1) Install
docs.text:
pip install arqon-pilot
pilot --help

docs.title: 2) Initialize and register repos
docs.text:
pilot init
pilot multi register --path /path/to/ArqonContinuum --group core --tag apply-pilot
pilot multi register --path /path/to/ArqonCortex --group core --tag apply-pilot
pilot multi status --tag apply-pilot

docs.title: 3) Run safe first operations
docs.text:
pilot branch create feat/pilot-rollout --group core --dry-run
pilot navigate --multi --group core --dry-run
pilot secure scan --group core
pilot secure fix --group core --dry-run

docs.title: Cross-repo branch orchestration
docs.text:
pilot multi order --group core
pilot branch create feat/my-change --group core --dry-run
pilot branch create feat/my-change --group core
pilot branch status --group core

docs.title: Coordinated release dry-run
docs.text: pilot navigate --multi --group core --dry-run

docs.title: Planning -> scaffold -> knowledge capture
docs.text:
pilot plan issues --input /tmp/issues.json
pilot plan score --input /tmp/issues.json --output /tmp/scored.json
pilot plan roadmap --input /tmp/scored.json --output /tmp/roadmap.md --top-n 10
pilot create feature checkout --dry-run
pilot know record --title "Wave decision" --context "Why" --decision "What" --tag wave

docs.title: Safety Model
docs.text:
• Run mutating commands with --dry-run before apply mode.
  • Use group/tag filters to reduce blast radius.
  • Keep worktrees clean before branch/navigate operations.
  • Review per-repo outcomes for partial failures before retrying.

docs.title: Common Gotchas
docs.text:
1. Dirty worktrees can block mutating cross-repo commands.
  2. Missing external tools (for specific scans/fixes) can reduce functionality.
  3. Dependency cycles in repo graph will fail ordered operations.
  4. If packaging fails, confirm Cargo.lock is committed and up to date.

docs.title: Arqon Ecosystem Branch Management Guide
docs.text: This document establishes the branch management standards and workflows for all repositories in the Arqon Ecosystem.

docs.title: Permanent branches
docs.text: Branch Purpose Protection Deploy status main Production-ready code Protected, requires PR Always deployable dev Integration branch Protected, requires PR Development builds

docs.title: Branch lifecycle
docs.text: feature/* -> dev -> main

docs.title: Branch relationships
docs.text:
• main is the source of truth for production.
  • dev is created from main and stays synchronized.
  • Feature branches are created from dev and merged back to dev.
  • dev -> main merges happen via PR when ready for release.

docs.title: Prefixes
docs.text: Prefix Purpose Example feat/ New feature feat/click-tones fix/ Bug fix fix/memory-leak docs/ Documentation only docs/api-reference test/ Test additions/changes test/integration-coverage refactor/ Code refactoring refactor/episode-parser chore/ Maintenance tasks chore/update-dependencies perf/ Performance improvements perf/query-optimization

docs.title: Naming rules
docs.text:
1. Use kebab-case after the prefix (feat/my-feature).
  2. Be descriptive and concise (3-5 words after the prefix).
  3. No issue numbers in branch names.
  4. For cross-repo features, use the same branch name across all affected repos.

docs.title: Branch TTL and cleanup SLA
docs.text:
• feat/*, fix/*, refactor/*, test/*, perf/*, chore/* branches should be merged, rebased, or closed within 14 days.
  • Branches older than 14 days must be either:
  • refreshed against dev and actively used, or
  • closed and recreated later.

docs.title: Standard feature flow
docs.text:
1. git checkout dev && git pull origin dev
  2. git checkout -b feat/my-feature
  3. Develop and commit.
  4. git push -u origin feat/my-feature
  5. Create PR feat/my-feature -> dev
  6. Merge PR.
  7. Delete branch locally/remotely.

PR requirements: - Include a Related PRs section for cross-repo work. - Include dependency order and rollback note in PR description.

docs.title: Hotfix flow
docs.text:
1. git checkout main && git pull origin main
  2. git checkout -b fix/critical-bug
  3. Fix and PR to main.
  4. Merge main back into dev.

docs.title: Release flow
docs.text:
1. Ensure dev is release-ready.
  2. PR dev -> main.
  3. Merge PR and tag from main.

Release tagging standard: - Use annotated SemVer tags: vX.Y.Z - Example: git tag -a v1.2.0 -m "Release v1.2.0" && git push origin v1.2.0

docs.title: Required steps
docs.text:
1. Plan affected repos and dependency order.
  2. Create consistent branch names across repos.
  3. Implement changes in dependency order.
  4. Create linked PRs with related references.
  5. Merge in dependency order.
  6. Update downstream dependencies after upstream merges.

Hard merge-order gate: - Do not merge downstream repo PRs before upstream dependency PRs are merged. - If order is violated, downstream PR must be revalidated after dependency update.

docs.title: Pilot command mapping
docs.text:
Use Arqon Pilot as the orchestration layer:

  1. Register and inspect workspace
  2. pilot multi register --path ... --group ... --tag ...
  3. pilot multi list

  4. pilot multi status

  5. Model dependency order

  6. pilot multi deps set --repo <repo> --depends-on <upstream>

  7. pilot multi order

  8. Coordinate branches

  9. pilot branch create <branch> --dry-run
  10. pilot branch sync --branch <branch> --dry-run
  11. pilot branch status

  12. pilot branch prune --dry-run

  13. Prepare linked release plan

  14. pilot multi prs create --dry-run

  15. pilot navigate --multi --dry-run

  16. Enforce merge order and tracking

  17. Add linked PR references in each PR body.
  18. Merge PRs in pilot multi order sequence.

docs.title: Decision 1: Branch protection rules
docs.text:
• main: require PR, require review, require CI pass.
  • dev: require PR, optional review, require CI pass.

Status: Confirmed.

docs.title: Decision 2: Direct commits to dev
docs.text:
• Policy: no direct commits; all changes via PR for traceability.

Status: Confirmed.

docs.title: Decision 3: Release branches
docs.text:
• Policy: no dedicated release/* branches by default; release from main tags.

Status: Confirmed.

docs.title: Decision 4: Documentation branch strategy
docs.text:
• Policy: hybrid.
  • Minor docs can ship with feature branches; major docs can use dedicated docs/*.

Status: Confirmed.

docs.title: Decision 5: Multi-repo sync strategy
docs.text:
• Policy: manual synchronization now; automate once CI maturity is sufficient.

Status: Confirmed.

docs.title: Decision 6: Protected branch exceptions
docs.text:
• Policy: emergency bypass of branch protection is allowed only for production incidents.
  • Requirements:
  • incident reference in commit/PR,
  • post-incident PR documenting final state,
  • retro entry in pilot know record.

Status: Confirmed.

docs.title: Rollback Policy
docs.text:
• Preferred rollback method: git revert (preserves audit history).
  • Avoid history-rewriting rollback on shared branches.
  • Before rollback:
  • capture current SHA and failing SHA,
  • record reason and impact,
  • execute rollback in dependency order for cross-repo incidents.

Emergency-only: - git reset --hard is local-recovery only and must not be used on shared/protected branches.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
1. Branch name mismatch across repos breaks linked-PR traceability.
  2. Repo name collisions in multi registry can map dependency edges incorrectly.
  3. Dirty local worktrees can produce false branch status or block safe apply flows.
  4. Merging out of dependency order creates hidden downstream breakage.
  5. Stale branches (>14 days) often miss upstream API or schema changes.
  6. Direct commits to dev bypass review/CI intent and create drift.
  7. Using reset-based rollback on shared branches destroys collaborative audit trail.
  8. Unlinked cross-repo PRs make incident triage and release signoff much slower.

docs.title: Compliance Checks
docs.text:
• Weekly branch hygiene report:
  • stale branches >14 days,
  • direct commits to protected branches,
  • PRs missing linked references for cross-repo work,
  • out-of-order merges against dependency graph.

docs.title: Daily
docs.text:
• git checkout dev && git pull origin dev
  • git checkout -b feat/my-feature
  • git status
  • git branch -vv

docs.title: Cleanup
docs.text:
• git branch -d feat/my-feature
  • git push origin --delete feat/my-feature
  • git fetch --prune

docs.title: Recovery
docs.text:
• git reflog
  • git checkout -b restored-branch <commit>

docs.title: ArqonPilot Operator Runbook
docs.text: This runbook defines the standard operating procedure for running Arqon Pilot across single-repo and multi-repo workflows.

docs.title: 1. Environment Baseline
docs.text:
• Rust toolchain pinned at 1.82.0 (rust-toolchain.toml).
  • Pilot binary built from current repo:
  • cargo build -p pilot
  • Workspace state path:
  • ~/.pilot/workspace.db
  • ~/.pilot/audit.jsonl
  • ~/.pilot/reports/*.json

docs.title: 2. Daily Safe Workflow (Dry-Run First)
docs.text:
1. Registry and health
  2. pilot multi list

  3. pilot multi status

  4. Dependency order and branch planning

  5. pilot multi order --group <group>
  6. pilot branch create feat/<name> --group <group> --base-branch dev --dry-run

  7. pilot branch sync --branch feat/<name> --group <group> --dry-run

  8. Release planning

  9. pilot multi prs create --group <group> --dry-run

  10. pilot navigate --multi --group <group> --dry-run

  11. Security and maintenance

  12. pilot secure scan --group <group>

  13. pilot secure fix --group <group> (dry-run default)

  14. Planning and knowledge loop

  15. pilot plan issues --input <issues.json>
  16. pilot plan score
  17. pilot plan roadmap
  18. pilot create feature <name> --dry-run
  19. pilot know record --title ... --context ... --decision ...

docs.title: 3. Controlled Apply Workflow
docs.text:
Apply mode is allowed only for explicitly tagged pilot cohorts.

  1. Pilot cohort registration

  2. pilot multi register --path <repo> --tag apply-pilot --tag wave7

  3. Preflight

  4. repo clean, on expected base branch, CI green, credentials available.

  5. Apply branch operation

  6. pilot branch create feat/<name> --tag apply-pilot --base-branch dev

  7. Apply secure fix (if desired)

  8. pilot secure fix --tag apply-pilot --apply

  9. Post-apply checks

  10. pilot branch status --tag apply-pilot
  11. repo tests and lint
  12. inspect ~/.pilot/audit.jsonl and ~/.pilot/reports/*.json

docs.title: 4. Rollback Procedure
docs.text:
Preferred rollback: - git revert <bad_commit_sha>

After rollback: 1. verify clean status 2. run tests 3. record incident and resolution via pilot know record

Avoid: - history rewriting on shared branches (reset --hard, force-push) except emergency local recovery with explicit approval.

docs.title: 5. Incident Triage
docs.text: When a multi-repo operation fails: 1. open latest report artifact from ~/.pilot/reports/ 2. isolate failing repo(s) 3. re-run command scoped to failed repo only 4. record root cause and corrective action in pilot know

docs.title: 6. Release Candidate Gate (v1-rc1)
docs.text: Before cutting pilot-v1-rc1: 1. cargo check -p pilot --locked 2. full CLI suite green 3. wave acceptance docs updated 4. dogfooding + controlled apply evidence documented 5. audit/report artifacts present and interpretable

docs.title: Testing Strategy
docs.text: Arqon Pilot uses five test layers to keep behavior stable as capabilities expand.

docs.title: Test Layers
docs.text:
1. Unit tests
  2. Scope: crate-local logic in src modules.

  3. Command: ./scripts/test_matrix.sh unit

  4. Integration tests

  5. Scope: CLI command groups and module boundaries.

  6. Command: ./scripts/test_matrix.sh integration

  7. End-to-end tests

  8. Scope: realistic multi-step flows across registered repos.

  9. Command: ./scripts/test_matrix.sh e2e

  10. Regression tests

  11. Scope: previously broken behavior that must never return.

  12. Command: ./scripts/test_matrix.sh regression

  13. Adversarial tests

  14. Scope: malformed input, cycle/failure isolation, and hostile edge cases.
  15. Command: ./scripts/test_matrix.sh adversarial

docs.title: Full Local Validation
docs.text:
./scripts/test_matrix.sh all
./scripts/release_readiness_check.sh

docs.title: CI Policy
docs.text:
• CI runs on Rust 1.82.0 for core checks.
  • PyPI packaging is a scoped exception with newer Rust in pypi.yml.
  • cargo --locked is required in release and packaging flows.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
1. If Cargo.lock is missing, builds may resolve incompatible crate versions.
  2. Adversarial failures should emit machine-readable --report-json output.
  3. E2E tests require local git available for temporary repos.
  4. Packaging can fail even when core CI passes; always run the TestPyPI lane.

docs.title: Decision

PyPI packaging will use maturin as the primary build/publish path.

  3. Supports repeatable CI publishing workflows.
